pr_body:
This PR piggy-backs on recent changes in Lucene 9.11.1 (https://github.com/apache/lucene/pull/12829, https://github.com/apache/lucene/pull/13341/), setting the parent doc when nested fields are present. This allows moving nested documents along with parent ones during sorting.

With this change, sorting is now allowed on fields outside nested objects. Sorting on fields within nested objects is still not supported (throws an exception).

Fixes #107349
pr_title: Support index sorting with nested fields
pr_comment: Hi @kkrik-es, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
This seems important enough, added a highlight note.

review_comment: I wonder if we need to keep this limitation for existing index? This would mean checking the index version to ensure that this mode is not activated on indices with an index sort and already indexed documents.
I see, the problem is that existing indexes do not have the parent field set and a mapping update may introduce a nested object. That's correct, we need to check for the version here.
I wonder how this works when the nested field is added as an update to the mapping? Should we always set the parent field in case a nested field is added later?
Good point, I was thinking about this but wasn't sure of the implications. @jpountz any thoughts on this?
I asked a similar question to @s1monw a while back, and he suggested always adding the parent field when an index sort is configured.
Excellent, this simplifies things. Lemme update the PR.
Maybe include the reason why parent field is always enabled in the comment too?
Right, this was added in the last iteration.
